title: Build HAL/Alfred routing helper script
description: Create a lightweight script to score tasks using HAL-ALFRED-ROUTING-PLAYBOOK thresholds and output route decision + triggers.

comments.author: alfred
comments.text:
Completed — hal-alfred-route.sh (242 lines) created at ~/.openclaw/workspace/scripts/

What it does:
- Deterministic routing engine based on HAL-ALFRED-ROUTING-PLAYBOOK
- Implements all 5 HAL gate checks: steps≤4, input_kb≤8, no external action, not high-risk, files≤6
- Keyword-triggered step bumping for complexity tasks (refactor, architecture, codegen, etc.)
- Confidence scoring (0.8–0.95) with band classification
- Supports --text, --steps, --input-kb, --files, --external, --risk, --json, --explain flags

Bug fixed: Complexity keywords now correctly bump step estimates (was routing "refactor auth" to HAL incorrectly)
All 5 test cases pass (HAL/parse, Alfred/refactor, explicit override, security risk, large input)

title: Implement auto-estimating HAL/Alfred routing wrapper
description: Build a wrapper that auto-estimates steps/input-kb/files from task text and optional file paths, then calls hal-alfred-route.sh.

comments.author: alfred
comments.text:
Completed — hal-alfred-route-auto.sh (218 lines) at ~/.openclaw/workspace/scripts/

What it does:
- Auto-estimates --steps from task text keywords (analyze +1, refactor +2, implement +2, security +2, etc.)
- Auto-estimates --input-kb from actual file sizes (reads provided files via --file arguments)
- Auto-estimates --files count from argument count
- Clamps steps 1–12 with length-based baseline (1 per 120 chars)
- Supports all playbook use cases: manual routing, explain mode, multi-file analysis
- Delegates to base router (hal-alfred-route.sh) with calculated parameters

All playbook use cases verified working.

comments.author: alfred
comments.text:
Completed — 3 new scripts + 1 playbook document created:

1. hal-alfred-track.sh (286 lines) — Decision logging to routing.jsonl. Commands: --decision (log), --outcome (update result), --summary, --stats (metrics dashboard)

2. hal-alfred-route-with-tracking.sh (110 lines) — Wrapper that auto-logs every routing decision. Auto-generates task IDs, shows track ID for cross-referencing

3. hal-alfred-report.sh (263 lines) — Metrics dashboard + tuning recommendations. Flags overconfidence, underconfidence, imbalanced volume. Recommends threshold adjustments per playbook section 8

4. HAL-ALFRED-ROUTING-PLAYBOOK.md (167 lines) — Full strategy document with 9 sections: ownership model, auto-routing rules, escalation triggers, return-downshift, task type matrix, handoff format, implementation phases, tuning targets, quick decision checklist

5 sample routing decisions already logged to routing.jsonl. Ready for Phase 1 measurement (20-task tracking cycle).
